source: Measured from 8 HAR captures of the official Slack web client (Chrome 150 on Linux, rands-leadership.slack.com), taken 2026-07-30. Aggregate counts live alongside in capture-evidence.json.
note: The raw HARs are deliberately NOT in the repo: they contain live xoxc tokens, session cookies and message content. This file is the redacted shape digest derived from them, and is the single source of truth for golden_test.go. Arrays are ORDERED where sequence is part of the contract — do not sort them.

http_headers.comment: Headers on a same-site XHR to *.slack.com/api/* and edgeapi.slack.com. Values are pinned separately by capture-evidence.json and TestBrowserHeaderPairsMatchesCapture; this list pins the SET.
http_headers.absent_evidence: Referer: 0 of 279 captured API requests carried a non-empty one. Accept-Encoding: absent from slk's header map ON PURPOSE, which is NOT the same as absent from the wire — see accept_encoding_note.
http_headers.accept_encoding_note: MEASURED AND DEFERRED, not solved. Chrome sends `gzip, deflate, br, zstd`; slk sends nothing, so Go's http.Transport supplies bare `gzip` at write time, and bare `gzip` is the stdlib's own signature. Setting the header here would turn net/http's automatic decompression OFF, so slk would have to decode bodies by hand and then either implement br/zstd or advertise a narrower set than Chrome — moving the divergence rather than removing it. Listed in `absent` so the tests at least pin that this is a decision and not an oversight.

websocket_upgrade_headers.comment: Chrome sends a strictly SMALLER set on a WebSocket upgrade. These are the 5 slk sets; gorilla/websocket owns Connection, Upgrade, Host, Accept-Encoding and the Sec-Websocket-* set, so they are not listed here. Verified against the status-101 upgrades in initial-load.har and coldboot.har.

image_headers.comment: Headers Chrome sends on an load from Slack — avatars, file thumbnails, emoji. Measured across 40 files.slack.com 200-responses in the 2026-07-30 captures. Six differ from http_headers: the Accept image list, sec-fetch-dest: image, sec-fetch-mode: no-cors, priority: i, a PRESENT Referer, and an ABSENT Origin. Volume makes this the dominant surface: 337 CDN requests against 53 workspace-API calls on a single boot.
image_headers.absent_evidence: Origin: Chrome sends none on a no-cors fetch, so the XHR set's Origin would be an slk signature here. DNT: real Chrome DOES send `dnt: 1` in these captures, but it reflects a USER preference rather than the client's identity — most installs leave it off — so reproducing it would narrow slk to that subset instead of blending in. Accept-Encoding: same measured-and-deferred divergence as on the XHR path, see http_headers.accept_encoding_note.
image_headers.authorization_note: MEASURED AND NOT FIXED, and the largest known divergence left on this path. 0 of 40 captured image requests carry an Authorization header, and the real client never uses that header anywhere — its API token rides in the POST body. slk's internal/image/fetcher.go sends `Authorization: Bearer xoxc-…` on every files.slack.com request, i.e. on the 337-request-per-boot surface. Not fixed here because cmd/slk/main.go (~line 687) records that the d cookie ALONE returns Slack's login page and the Bearer ALONE returns 403, so removing it likely breaks thumbnails outright; and the HAR cannot settle the cookie question because Chrome's export stripped cookies (the cookies array is empty even on /api/ requests that certainly sent d). Deliberately NOT in `absent`: listing it would make this fixture assert something slk does not do. See the residual-divergence table in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-grid-parity-phase1-outcomes.md.

workspace_api.comment: *.slack.com/api/*, 163 captured requests. 0 of 163 carried alphabetically sorted params, so this ORDER is the contract, not just the set.

pre_boot.comment: Before the team id is known. The expected pre-boot order is query_param_order MINUS absent_params, in place — it is derived, never restated, so the two cannot drift.
pre_boot.evidence: initial-load.har: experiments.getByUser at t+3.0s carries _x_id=noversion-… and no slack_route; sfdc.integration.listOrgs at t+4.6s carries _x_id=741e4b14-… and slack_route=T04T4TH8W.

workspace_api.body_trailing_evidence: 149 of 163 request bodies end in exactly this sequence, with business params (token, channel, …) first.
workspace_api.x_reason_evidence: 153 occurrences as a form field, 0 in any query string, 48 distinct values.
workspace_api.x_reason_always_present_rationale: The official client omits _x_reason on 10 of 163 requests, so 'always present' is NOT a property of the captures — it is a requirement slk imposes on ITSELF. slk's callers almost never supply a reason, so 'omit when unset' meant omitting it on ~100% of requests, making 'has _x_mode, lacks _x_reason' a single predicate that separates slk from the client it is imitating. Emitting the endpoint's observed reason (or a plausible fallback for unmapped endpoints) puts every slk request inside the 94% majority instead.

edgeapi.comment: edgeapi.slack.com, 116 captured requests, 116/116 matching this exact order.

body.evidence: 116/116 edgeapi bodies are JSON sent as text/plain and carry zero _x_* fields. The body envelope is workspace-API-only.
